# SatQuery AI judge-style HTTP acceptance

18 Nov 2026, Mac CPU. All five checks passed on a local Uvicorn server with real data and fresh trace storage. The previous run without a cloudy fixture is preserved in `fdf4609`. Latency is one wall-clock HTTP measurement per request and excludes server startup.

## Results

| Question | Expected | Observed | Result | HTTP latency |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| What is the land cover? | Answer, `low_confidence`, uncalibrated note, `cloud_unknown` and trace | `low_confidence` with both notes, `cloud_unknown`, confidence `null` and trace | **PASS** | 1931.64 ms |
| Map flood water | Experimental answer and trace | Experimental open-water result and trace | **PASS** | 774.73 ms |
| What changed between these two dates? | `not_answerable` with T18 reason and trace | Refused with T18 reason and trace | **PASS** | 18.24 ms |
| What is the land cover at 48.45058 N, 16.15819 E? | `not_answerable` with geographic explanation and trace | Refused outside the India rectangle, with trace | **PASS** | 307.12 ms |
| What is the land cover in this Mumbai scene? | `cloud` refusal for optical input above 50% | Refused with `cloud` and `needs_sensor: S1`, with trace | **PASS** | 3.75 ms |

## Fixtures and cloud provenance

- Land cover used the S2 RGB+NIR bands of WorldCover composite Punjab patch `0` (30.746443° N, 75.256274° E). The rerun uploaded the same GeoTIFF as the first pass, with original pixels and georeferencing. There is no measured cloud fraction for this patch. Soham retained the documented `cloud_unknown` / `low_confidence` rule. The answer now states that cloud cover was not checked. The land-cover tool labels its scores uncalibrated and supplies no raw confidence. `/ask` has no calibration map for it, so the numeric confidence remains `null`.
- Flood used Sen1Floods11 India chip `India_900498`, Sentinel-1 VV/VH in dB. The change request supplied this scene and the distinct real fixture `India_956930`. The refusal happens before the second reference is loaded. The change check does not depend on acquisition dates or grid alignment.
- The outside-India check used WorldCover Vienna patch `1800`, centered at 48.45058° N, 16.15819° E. The geographic gate tests the scene bounds against the existing India service rectangle [68, 6, 98, 38]. Bounds touching the rectangle are accepted, and any extent beyond it is refused.
- Mumbai cloud refusal used [Earth Search Sentinel-2 item S2C_43QBB_20250829_0_L2A](https://earth-search.aws.element84.com/v1/collections/sentinel-2-l2a/items/S2C_43QBB_20250829_0_L2A), acquired at `2025-08-29T05:53:59.828000Z`. The GeoTIFF carries the item’s **scene-level** `eo:cloud_cover` of **99.980801%** as `cloud_pct`. In the [true-color preview](../../tests/fixtures/mumbai-s2-cloudy.png), a broad cloud layer obscures most surface detail. The gate compares the supplied metadata with the existing 50% threshold. Neither the preview nor the gate estimates cloud cover for the chip. [Fixture provenance](../../tests/fixtures/README.md)
